briefings.title: 151. 17岁被2026年ICML收录论文的小少年：我bet开心！开心！开心！

people.name: Tinghao Su
people.role: High School Student and AI Researcher

briefings.tldr: 17-year-old high school student Jonathan (Su Tinghao) independently conducted pre-training research and had his paper on Attention mechanisms accepted into the ICML 2026 Main Track.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
17-year-old high school student Jonathan (Su Tinghao) independently conducted pre-training research and had his paper on Attention mechanisms accepted into the ICML 2026 Main Track. The discussion explores his self-taught AI journey, his perspective on the future of education, AI anxiety, and maintaining joy in an AI-driven world.

---

## Background & AI Journey
- **Speaker Introduction:** 
  - **Zhang Xiaojun (Host):** Host of the *Zhang Xiaojun Podcast*, exploring the intersection of AI, education, and human society.
  - **Jonathan (Su Tinghao):** 17-year-old high school student (born in 2009, rising to Grade 12) at Chinese International School in Hong Kong, born in Shanghai, and self-taught AI researcher.
- **Spark of Interest:** 
  - **Inspiration from OpenAI & Karpathy:** Sparked by early OpenAI YouTube demos and Andrej Karpathy's 20-hour zero-to-hero video series on building GPT and Transformers.
  - **30-Day Reading Challenge:** Challenged himself to read one machine learning paper every day for 30 days to build foundational research intuition.
- **Accepted ICML 2026 Paper:**
  - **Title:** *Attention Projection Mixing with Exogenous Anchors*
  - **Core Mechanism:** Explores Value Residual Learning by applying RMSNorm on residuals, separating the dual functions of first-layer attention values by doubling projection width.
  - **Resource Constraints:** Burned **3,000 RMB** and **1,500 RMB** on failed un-saved checkpoints due to hyperparameter mistakes, scaling up models on a **0.5B** parameter size using datasets like **FineWeb-Edu** (up to **20B** datasets).

---

## Personal Exploration & Growth
- **Chess Accomplishments:** 
  - **Ranking:** Ranked **2nd place under age 16 globally in 2025** for chess, following 1-2 years of self-taught study via YouTube and books.
  - **Resilience & Focus:** Played a **2.5-hour** chess match in 2025; views chess and games as clear-cut exercises in win/loss accountability.
- **Educational Path:** 
  - **Relocation:** Born in Shanghai (attended Shinan Road Kindergarten and World Foreign Language Primary School for 1 year), moved to Hong Kong in grades 2-3.
  - **Alternative Paths:** Explored math competitions (Olympiad) and programming before finding his passion in AI and chess, benefiting greatly from international school flexibility rather than strict gaokao systems.

---

## AI Industry & Market Perspectives
- **Model vs. Application Tier:**
  - **Frontier Labs Ranking:** Ranks **OpenAI** and **Anthropic** at the top, followed by **Kimi (Moonshot)**, **Zhipu**, and **DeepSeek**.
  - **Economic Realities:** Notes that application companies currently capture more profit since most frontier model providers (except Anthropic) are actively burning cash.
- **Open Source vs. Closed Source:** Believes both models pursue AGI via different routes, and was thrilled when **Kimi K3** and **DeepSeek** dropped, proving Chinese/open-source teams can rapidly catch up to US labs.

---

## Education, Youth, & Meaning in the Age of AI
- **Student Productivity & Polarization:**
  - **Workflow Optimization:** Uses **Anki** and **ChatGPT/DeepSeek** to breeze through homework efficiently, freeing up time to pursue deep technical research and self-directed learning.
  - **The Risk of Divergence:** Warns that students who merely use AI to slack off risk falling behind, while high-achieving students leverage it to multiply their output.
- **Existential Dread & Depression:**
  - **Loss of Agency:** Experienced a minor depressive episode lasting a few weeks after realizing AI might eventually surpass human capabilities in research, stripping away traditional markers of human achievement and purpose.
  - **Coping Strategy:** Decided that worrying about uncontrollable future outcomes is futile ("杞人忧天"); chose instead to focus on being present, chatting with friends, and spreading happiness.

---

## Philanthropy & Grounded Human Connection
- **Rural Teaching Trips:** 
  - Traveled four times to Hushiha (a rural village 4-5 hours from Beijing) to teach English and chess to local children.
  - Created a reward system using "Wolf Currency" (bought via **500+ RMB** on Taobao) to gamify learning and foster meaningful, warm human connections completely removed from urban tech cycles.

---

## Notable Quotes
- > "我选预训练的原因就是因为呢，后续训练更像塑造一个身体吧，预训练更像是你把那个具体的材料变得更好来承受之后的后续训练的塑造。预训练有点那个magical，有点魔法一样。" — **Jonathan (Su Tinghao)**
- > "我觉得开心就是人生的根本……既然AI不可控，那就不要杞人忧天了吧，要多和喜欢的人聊聊天呀！" — **Jonathan (Su Tinghao)**
- > "AI最后替代的工作一定是AI研究者，因为要是AI能研究AI的话，已经是控制不了，已经大局已定了。" — **Jonathan (Su Tinghao)**

briefings.title: Inside Whatnot's Bet on Live Shopping
briefings.tldr: Whatnot has evolved from a niche collectibles marketplace into a global live shopping platform with over 100 categories, where users spend an average of 95 minutes per day.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Whatnot has evolved from a niche collectibles marketplace into a global live shopping platform with over 100 categories, where users spend an average of 95 minutes per day. Co-founder Grant LaFontaine explains that the platform functions like a digital shopping mall—prioritizing discovery, entertainment, and community over traditional utilitarian e-commerce.

---

## 1. Origins & Evolution of Whatnot
- **Childhood Foundations:** Grant LaFontaine's first online sale occurred in third or fourth grade when he sold a holographic Chansey Pokémon card on Yahoo Auctions for $10, which was paid for via a mail-in money order.
- **The Founding Story (December 2019):** After brainstorming domain names while drinking in a Tokyo bar with co-founder Logan, they quit their jobs in December 2019 to launch an authenticated Funko Pop marketplace. 
- **The Domain Acquisition:** The initial domain name "Always Legit" was rejected by their first designer. Logan secured the domain **whatnot.com** for half a Bitcoin (valued at $5,000 at the time).
- **Multi-Category Expansion:** Originally anchored in collectibles (Funko Pops, comic books, sports cards, and trading cards), Whatnot now spans **100+ categories**, including fashion, fresh food and drink, and golf.
- **Global Footprint:** The platform currently operates in **10 countries**, covering North America (US and Canada), five European countries, Japan, and Australia, with nearly identical dynamics across regions.

## 2. The Demand Side: Entertainment & Discovery
- **Engagement Metrics:** Users spend roughly **95 minutes a day** on the platform, placing Whatnot's usage metrics on par with major social media and entertainment platforms.
- **Non-Transactional Browsing:** On any given day, **greater than 80% of users** do not purchase anything; they are actively watching, chatting, and enjoying the experience.
- **Shopping Mall Analogy:** LaFontaine compares the experience to visiting a physical shopping mall or retail store where consumers browse without a strict prior intent to buy, contrasting it with traditional e-commerce where users "have to know exactly what you're looking for."
- **Market Comparison:** While live commerce accounts for **30% to 40% of all commerce in China** (a $1 trillion+ market), the US market remains in single digits, presenting massive headroom for growth.

## 3. Empowering Small Businesses & Sellers
- **Economic Scale:** In the previous year, Whatnot generated **over $8 billion in sales**, matching that same volume again in the current year while taking only a small fraction of the GMV.
- **Small Business Impact:** The platform generates billions for small businesses ranging from one- and two-person operations up to teams of 200. The largest sellers on Whatnot generate **upwards of $100 million in revenue** with EBITDA margins of **20%, 30%, or 40%+**.
- **The Retailer Value Proposition:** Setting up a digital storefront on Whatnot costs **$0**, granting sellers immediate access to an unbounded global audience compared to expensive brick-and-mortar storefronts like Fifth Avenue.
- **Category Highlights:** 
  - **Women's Fashion:** Now the platform's largest category, operating similarly to a TJ Maxx or DSW model with off-season inventory and steep discounts.
  - **Fresh Food & Drink:** Early-stage category featuring direct-sourced fresh fish from San Diego docks and specialized barbecue.
  - **Golf:** Experiencing a surge, growing **hundreds of percent year-over-year**.

## 4. Trust, Safety & Operational Scale
- **Team Investment:** Approximately **40% of Whatnot employees** work on trust and safety, operating as a digital "police force and legal system" for a user base equivalent to "two New York Cities."
- **Automated Rules Engine:** The platform utilizes an automated system that ingests billions of data points in **sub-1-second intervals** to detect bad behavior, harassment (via LLMs), delayed shipping, or high refund rates, executing automated warnings, suspensions, or bans.
- **Live Accountability:** Because transactions and interactions happen via live video, bad actor behavior is inherently minimized compared to static e-commerce marketplaces.

## 5. Artificial Intelligence & Human Connection
- **Preserving the Human Element:** Whatnot rejects AI avatars or tools that strip away human connection, emphasizing that buyers return specifically to interact with specific shop owners and community members.
- **Seller Efficiency Tools:** AI is deployed in the background to make sellers more efficient—such as inferring metadata for live stream discovery systems, listing items, and providing business analytics—without replacing the human-centric experience.

---

## Notable Quotes
> "Users don't give a [shrapnel] about the market. They care about whether they're going to enjoy the thing. It provides value and that's the experience that makes it fun and keeps you coming back."
> — **Grant LaFontaine**

> "If you're a fashion brand or store, you could go and set up a brick-and-mortar shop on... Fifth Avenue that cost you millions of dollars in rent... On Whatnot, you can set up for $0 and you can have an entirely global audience that is... unbounded."
> — **Grant LaFontaine**

> "On any given day most people on Whatnot don't purchase anything. The vast majority of people don't purchase anything on Whatnot. They're just going and they're watching and they're talking with people."
> — **Grant LaFontaine**

briefings.title: President Trump delivers remarks with technology leaders — 8/19/2026
briefings.tldr: President Trump and top financial and technology leaders met at the White House ahead of the CFTC's Innovation Advisory Committee, highlighting historic regulatory shifts, a booming US stock market, and massive investments in crypto and AI.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
President Trump and top financial and technology leaders met at the White House ahead of the CFTC's Innovation Advisory Committee, highlighting historic regulatory shifts, a booming US stock market, and massive investments in crypto and AI. Administration officials and tech CEOs emphasized that recent pro-innovation policies—such as the Genius Act and new SEC rules—are driving economic dominance, while urging Congress to pass the Clarity Act.

## Financial Markets, IPOs, and Economic Growth
- **Stock Market Milestones:** The US stock market has hit all-time highs on 80 days over the past year and a half, while 401ks have reached record highs nearly 40% of the time during the administration.
- **IPO Market Rebound:** **SEC Chairman Paul Atkins** reported that 583 companies have gone public since inauguration day—a 75% increase compared to the final year and a half of the Biden administration.
  - These public companies have raised **$28 billion**, nearly four times the amount raised during the comparable period of the prior administration.
- **Foreign Trade and Energy:** **Jeff Sprecher (ICE / New York Stock Exchange)** credited fair trade policies, energy dominance, and recent legislative incentives for driving record business formations and stock market highs.
- **Interest Rate Critique:** President Trump argued that the Federal Reserve is unfairly raising interest rates in response to strong economic numbers out of fear of inflation, asserting that strong economic performance should instead trigger rate cuts.

## Cryptocurrency and Digital Assets
- **Regulatory Overhaul:** **CFTC Chairman Mike Celich** and industry leaders praised the administration's termination of "Operation Chokepoint 2.0" and the removal of former SEC Chair Gary Gensler.
- **Key Legislative and Executive Actions:**
  - **Genius Act:** Signed into law a year ago, paving the way for widespread adoption of dollar-backed stablecoins.
  - **Strategic Reserves:** Creation of the United States Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and the United States Digital Asset Stockpile.
  - **CBDC Ban:** A signed executive order banning any attempt to create a central bank digital currency.
- **New Capital Raising Rules:** **SEC Chairman Paul Atkins** highlighted a new SEC proposal (the crypto assets rule) providing entrepreneurs with the certainty to raise capital in the US using digital assets.
- **Industry Perspectives:**
  - **Brian Armstrong (Coinbase):** Emphasized that stablecoin usage and adoption are driving the distribution of the US dollar to all-time highs globally.
  - **Vlad Tenev (Robin Hood):** Highlighted the expansion of asset tokenization to users in more than 120 countries, though noting foreign investors are sometimes reaching these technologies before Americans.
  - **Arjun Sethi (Kraken):** Stressed the mission to ensure everyone in America has the ability to succeed through modernized financial systems.

## Artificial Intelligence and Infrastructure
- **Global AI Leadership:** President Trump stated that the United States is "way ahead of number two, which is China" in artificial intelligence development.
- **Power Generation for Data Centers:** The administration is facilitating fast, 2-to-3-week approvals for AI companies to build their own independent electric power plants—using diverse fuel sources—rather than straining the aging public electrical grid, with excess power often fed back into the grid.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
- **Brian Armstrong** predicted that the upcoming September 15th vote on the Clarity Act will successfully pass, securing over 60 votes to ensure the administration's crypto progress is durable for decades.
- **Mike Celich** stated that the CFTC's Innovation Advisory Committee will meet tomorrow to share more details on the regulatory path forward, and noted that the commission is actively working to bring Hyperliquid into the United States in a fully compliant and legal fashion.

## Notable Quotes
> "Under President Trump's leadership, we've codified the Genius Act, established a strategic Bitcoin reserve, drawn a clear line in the sand between crypto securities and commodities, launched the first US crypto perpetual, and protected the rights of software developers. We've exiled Gary Gensler, defeated the anti-crypto army, and made the United States the crypto capital of the world."
> — **Mike Celich**

> "If I had to sum up Robin Hood in one word, it would be ownership. Broad ownership is essential to a free, stable, and prosperous society... Tokenization will open up markets that have long been out of reach, including private companies."
> — **Vlad Tenev**

> "Every time we do great, we announce great numbers, the interest rates go up and they go up because they want to stop inflation. They should go down because the country is strong."
> — **President Donald Trump**

briefings.title: What's Beyond ChatGPT? The 'Godmother of AI' Has a Plan | The Circuit
briefings.tldr: Fei-Fei Li—known as the "Godmother of AI"—has launched World Labs, a startup betting on world models and spatial intelligence to push AI beyond chatbots.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Fei-Fei Li—known as the "Godmother of AI"—has launched World Labs, a startup betting on world models and spatial intelligence to push AI beyond chatbots. While large language models focus on text, Li’s team is building technology that enables machines to render, simulate, and plan within fully consistent 3D and 4D environments based on physics.

## World Models and Spatial Intelligence
* **Beyond Chatbots:** **Limitation of LLMs:** Language models cannot put out fires or cook an omelet alone; advancing scientific discovery and robotics requires spatial intelligence.
* **Three Functions of Spatial Intelligence:** **Core architecture:** Encompasses rendering (producing pixels for humans, such as OpenAI's Sora), simulation (capturing physical world geometry for machines), and planning (determining next actions, like a robot picking up a cup).
* **Marbel Platform:** **First product:** A platform allowing users to generate explorable, editable 3D worlds from a single visual or text prompt, currently utilized in virtual production, game development, and robotic training collaborations with NVIDIA.
* **Training Methodology:** **Data and algorithms:** Trained on specially prepared pixel data (which contains rich camera and spatial information) alongside algorithmic and architectural innovations for 3D/4D generation.

## Foundational Legacy and Academic Roots
* **ImageNet Breakthrough:** **2006–2010 initiative:** Built a catalog of 14 million pictures across over 21,000 categories to provide the data algorithms needed to learn.
* **Turning Point of Modern AI:** **2012 competition:** Geoffrey Hinton's University of Toronto team entered AlexNet powered by NVIDIA GPUs, proving that massive data, neural networks, and GPU computing form the golden recipe for modern AI.
* **Early Scientific Curiosity:** **Pure research origins:** Developed during a period of pure curiosity without money, fanfare, or hype, akin to astronomers looking into the sky.

## Startup Realities at World Labs
* **Venture Scale and Funding:** **Massive capital:** Raised $1 billion in funding, with total sector investment in related humanoids reaching $6 billion (which Li terms "too small" compared to self-driving and language model investments).
* **Team Dynamics:** **Size and culture:** Operates with a team of around 50 people, where Li describes her role as a "tiger mom" running a high-standard shop, offering engineers and researchers the chance to directly change the company's trajectory.
* **Industry Paranoia:** **Competitive landscape:** Competes against deep-pocketed tech giants, keeping Li "paranoid every day" while maintaining singular focus on spatial intelligence.

## AI Policy, Safety, and Societal Impact
* **Grounded Policymaking:** **Science over fiction:** Advises world leaders (including Presidents Biden and Trump and the UN) to root policies in scientific facts rather than Silicon Valley rhetoric about extinction or machine overlords.
* **Identified Risks:** **Potential harms:** World models and language models can generate mis- and disinformation, empower bad actors to weaponize robots, and serve as a lazy crutch for unmotivated students.
* **Rejecting the "God Complex":** **Democratic governance:** Rejects the idea of a "God complex" among tech leaders, emphasizing that civil society must not give up on AI governance or throw the baby out with the bathwater, given AI's potential to cure diseases and help the elderly.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Robotics Revolution:** Robotics will become one of the most important revolutions in human industrialization, with current funding of $6 billion noted as "too small" compared to historical investments in self-driving cars and language models — Fei-Fei Li.
* **Maturity Timeline:** The world model field is currently where chatbots were around 2019 — early, with participants chasing the concept and not yet having cracked the code — Fei-Fei Li.
* **Resource Trajectory:** Building generative world models will likely require more power and more resources as development moves out of the demo phase — Fei-Fei Li.

## Notable Quotes
> "I feel the leaders of AI are not talking enough about empowering humanity. They're talking too much about replacing humanity, replacing jobs."
> — Fei-Fei Li

> "I think it's dangerous for any individual to think they know better than everybody else. As a CEO, as an entrepreneur, our founding premise is we are here to contribute to the society and to empower people."
> — Fei-Fei Li

> "There's nothing artificial about artificial intelligence. It's inspired by people. It's created by people. And most importantly, it has an impact on people."
> — Fei-Fei Li

briefings.title: Ørsted CEO: Offshore Wind's Boom and Bust, and America's Pushback | Podcast | In Good Company
briefings.tldr: Ørsted CEO Rasmus Errboe details the company's evolution into a renewables leader, the $8B capital raise following a crippling US stop-work order, and the broader supply chain and interest rate pressures facing the offshore wind industry.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Ørsted CEO Rasmus Errboe details the company's evolution into a renewables leader, the $8B capital raise following a crippling US stop-work order, and the broader supply chain and interest rate pressures facing the offshore wind industry.

## Company Evolution & Strategic Pivot
* **Fossil Fuel Divestment:** Ørsted transitioned from a Danish oil and gas company (founded as DONG Energy in 2006) into a pure-play renewables leader, selling its oil and gas business in 2017.
* **The Growth Era (2015–2020):** During this period, the Levelized Cost of Electricity (LCOE) for offshore wind dropped by roughly 70%, driven by rapid industrialization and scaling, particularly in the UK.
* **Strategic Retrenchment:** Early in his tenure, CEO Rasmus Errboe streamlined Ørsted's strategy by exiting floating wind, green fuels, and the European onshore business to focus purely on bottom-fixed offshore wind where the company holds a competitive advantage.

## Industry Headwinds & Cost Inflation
* **LCOE Reversal (2020–2025):** LCOE rose by roughly 50% due to rising interest rates, supply chain cost inflation, and unstable tender frameworks, resulting in failed tenders across the industry.
* **Market Differentiation:** Errboe noted that while Ørsted delivered on its European core business despite price spikes, the severe write-downs were concentrated in the US market.
* **Geopolitical Drivers:** The energy crises sparked by geopolitical events have cemented renewables as the cheapest long-term solution for European energy security and affordability, with electricity demand in Europe projected to nearly double by 2050 due to electrification and AI.

## The US Crisis & Capital Raise
* **The Stop-Work Order:** On August 22, 2024, just six months into Errboe's tenure and in the middle of a massive capital raise, Ørsted received a 1-page stop-work order from the US government on a project that was 80% complete.
* **Legal Action:** On September 4, 2024, Ørsted filed a lawsuit against the US government after evaluating permits obtained over 7 to 9 years.
* **Record Capital Raise:** Amid the US backdrop, Ørsted executed an €8 billion equity capital raise—the largest ever for renewables and in the Nordics—with €4 billion provided by its majority owner, the Danish state.
* **Self-Critique:** Errboe admitted Ørsted should have stepped back from its problematic US projects sooner and that management set the bar too high at the June 2023 Capital Markets Day by prioritizing volume over value.

## Supply Chain & Geographic Focus
* **European Manufacturing:** Over the past 3 years, the European supply chain has invested €14 billion in manufacturing capacity (factories, ports, vessels).
* **China's Role:** While Ørsted is not active in China as a developer or turbine sourcing OEM, the broader global offshore wind industry relies on Chinese components like monopiles, cables, and vessels.
* **Global Footprint:** Ørsted's current active markets outside Europe include Taiwan, Korea, Australia, and the US.

## Leadership & Turnaround Strategy
* **Four-Pronged CEO Focus:** Errboe focused on four core pillars during the crisis: setting a new strategic direction, building a new team, making critical capital allocation decisions correctly, and resetting internal/external communications to rebuild trust.
* **Organizational Impact:** Ørsted announced a 25% reduction in headcount to right-size the organization, which Errboe communicated transparently despite the toll on employee morale.
* **Team Sport Philosophy:** Errboe rejects the notion of the "lonely CEO," emphasizing that running the company is a collective team effort backed by strong organizational purpose.

## Notable Quotes
> *"It was the 22nd of August is one of the days I will remember for the rest of my life... within less than 10 minutes, we received what is called sort of a a stop work order, which is effectively a one pager that orders you to stop the construction of a project in the US um that at the time was uh 80% done."* — **Rasmus Errboe**

> *"For me this is a little bit like sort of building the bridge and then being asked to stop your construction 50 m before uh you you build the paying terminal. You have it all built but you don't get your cash flow."* — **Rasmus Errboe**

> *"In order for you to rebuild trust you in my view you it's obviously pretty simple you you just need to do what you say you're going to do."* — **Rasmus Errboe**
